He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's Hawks]]. ==Early life and high school== Brown was born in [[Philadelphia]], Pennsylvania and grew up in the [[Northeast Philadelphia|northeast]] section of the city. He initially attended [[Imhotep Institute Charter High School]] before transferring to [[George Washington High School (Philadelphia)|George Washington High School]] before his junior year. Before his senior year he played for Philly Pride in the [[Amateur Athletic Union]].{{Cite web|last=Breen|first=Matt|title=Philly’s Charlie Brown Jr. is getting a chance with the Sixers — and serving as the ‘perfect story’ for an imperfect NBA season|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/charlie-brown-jr-sixers-saint-josephs-phil-martelli-20220111.html|url-status=live|access-date=2022-01-16|website=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220111162543/https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/charlie-brown-jr-sixers-saint-josephs-phil-martelli-20220111.html |archive-date=January 11, 2022 }} As a senior, Brown averaged 18.4 points per game and was named the MVP [[Philadelphia Public League]]'s B Division. He verbally committed to [[West Chester University]] but was offered and accepted a scholarship to [[Saint Joseph's University]]. Brown opted to prep for a fifth year at the [[St. Thomas More School (Connecticut)|St. Thomas More School]] in [[Oakdale, Connecticut]], where he helped the team to a 31–6 record and the National Prep Championship game.{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/ncaa/saint-josephs-doubles-down-recruits|title=Saint Joseph's doubles down on recruits|website=[[NBC Sports Philadelphia]]|date=November 18, 2015|access-date=June 23, 2019|archive-date=June 24, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190624004307/https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/ncaa/saint-josephs-doubles-down-recruits|url-status=live}} ==College career== [[File:Charlie Brown St. Joes.jpg|thumb|left|Brown with [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's]] in November 2016]] As a freshman at [[Saint Joseph's University|Saint Joseph's]], he started 30 of the Hawks' 31 games and averaged 12.8 points, five rebounds, and 1.1 assists while shooting 38.4 percent from behind the arc and 81.9 percent from the free-throw line. Brown was named to the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] All-Rookie team.{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/saint-josephs-hawks/st-joes-charlie-brown-out-few-weeks-broken-wrist|title=St. Joe's Charlie Brown out a few weeks with broken wrist|website=[[NBC Sports Philadelphia]]|date=October 25, 2017|access-date=June 23, 2019|archive-date=June 23, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190623220945/https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/saint-josephs-hawks/st-joes-charlie-brown-out-few-weeks-broken-wrist|url-status=live}} He was named third team all conference entering his true sophomore season, but missed the entirety of the year after being forced to use a medical [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] after breaking his wrist in preseason practice.{{cite web|url=https://www.phillytrib.com/sports/key-players-benched-by-injuries-return-to-excite-st-joseph/article_5df86de2-6bd7-5040-afea-e846e58a4355.html|title=Key players, sidelined by injuries, return to excite St. Joseph's|first=Donald|last=Hunt|work=[[Philadelphia Tribune]]|date=November 9, 2018|access-date=June 23, 2019|archive-date=June 23, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190623220935/https://www.phillytrib.com/sports/key-players-benched-by-injuries-return-to-excite-st-joseph/article_5df86de2-6bd7-5040-afea-e846e58a4355.html|url-status=live}} As a redshirt sophomore, Brown led the Atlantic 10 with 19.0 points per game and averaged 6.2 rebounds and 1.5 assists over 32 games earning him second team All-Atlantic 10 and first team All-[[Philadelphia Big 5|Big 5]] honors. In total, Brown scored 1,006 points and grabbed 352 rebounds in 63 games during his college career.{{cite web|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/charlie-brown-st-josephs-darius-bazley-philadelphia-76ers-sixers-predraft-workouts-20190617.html|title=Former St. Joe's standout Charlie Brown to work out for [[Julius Randle]], and one Lottery Protected first-round pick. The Hornets also received [[DaQuan Jeffries]], [[Duane Washington Jr.]], three second-round picks and draft compensation. New York acquired [[Karl-Anthony Towns]] and the draft rights to [[James Nnaji]].{{cite web|title=Hornets Acquire Three Picks, Three Players In Three-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-acquire-three-picks-three-players-in-three-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=October 2, 2024|access-date=October 2, 2024}} However, on October 18, he was waived by the Hornets.{{cite web|title=Hornets Waive Brown, Giles And Johnson|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-waive-brown-giles-and-johnson|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2024|access-date=October 20, 2024}} ===Raptors 905 (2024–2025)=== On October 28, 2024, Brown joined the [[Raptors 905]].{{cite tweet|author=Raptors 905|title=Welcome to the team, Charlie Brown Jr. 🤝|number=1851036469105696779|user=Raptors905|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}} On November 19, he tied the G-League record for most steals in a game by recording 9 steals in a 109–119 loss against the [[Capital City Go-Go]]. This record was broken 20 days later by Isaac Nogués of the [[Rip City Remix]] who set the new record by recording 10 in a game against the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]]. === Memphis Hustle (2025–2026) ===
